Write section titles in cards with a brief explanation (2-3 sentence) here. put inside big div container, flex row, with huge gap example section card: export function NewComponent() {  return (   
     

        HERO SECTION     

     

        Neptune is sunsetting.       

        Your experiments don't have to.     

     

        Migrate your ML experiment tracking to Pluto — a maintained, high-performance alternative with dual-logging support for a seamless transition.     

   
  )} rainy — Landing Page Structure 1. Hero Tagline: GPU infra, solved. Subtitle: Everything between buying GPUs and shipping models. Visual: YAML config snippet (simplified workload.yaml) → 3 mini-cards fanning out below: Training — multi-node status, GPU count Inference — endpoint live, autoscaling Experiment Tracking — mini loss curve (Pluto) CTAs: Book a Demo (primary) · Try Pluto Playground (secondary) Social proof strip: YC badge · customer logos · "5M+ GPU hours managed" · "50% cost savings" 2. "You bought GPUs. Now what?" Short problem statement — 2-3 lines max: Your team is spending weeks on scheduling, networking, and health checks instead of research. Or overpaying a managed platform to avoid it. Either way, your GPUs aren't working as hard as your team. 3. "Scale training across hundreds of GPUs" Multi-node distributed training with RDMA-native networking. Define workloads in YAML, launch from CLI, zero code changes. Priority-based scheduling — your most important jobs always run first. Built-in health checks validate GPU and networking performance before training begins, catching hardware issues before they waste compute. Automatic fault detection and recovery — failed jobs restart on healthy nodes, even at 3am. Works with PyTorch, HuggingFace, JAX, Ray, and more. Stat: "50% cost savings vs SageMaker" (Causal Labs) Visual: Job queue + allocation dashboard (similar to existing graphic — jobs queued, active/pending status, GPU allocation). 4. "Deploy and serve models" Inference scheduling on the same cluster, same YAML interface. Deploy serving endpoints with the same config-driven workflow used for training. Autoscaling, health checks, same reliability guarantees. One platform for training and inference means no context-switching between tools, no separate infra to manage. Visual: Endpoint status card, green dot, autoscaling indicator. 5. "Track every experiment without the lag" Pluto — experiment tracking built for responsiveness at scale. Sub-second UI even with thousands of runs and heavy time-series logging. The dashboard that doesn't slow down when your project gets big. Neptune-compatible API — swap one import line, keep your existing code Dual-logging — run Neptune and Pluto side-by-side, validate before cutting over MCP integration — query experiments through Claude instead of manual dashboard digging Open source — Apache 2 client, GPL server. Self-host in ~1 minute with docker-compose, or use managed hosting. Visual: Screenshot of Pluto dashboard or live playground embed. CTA: Try the Playground 6. "Launch your first job in 20 minutes" The developer experience section. Three steps: Write your config file — Specify nodes, priority, and GPU types in one simple YAML file. Deploy with one command — Launch your job with a single CLI command. We handle networking, scaling, and fault recovery. Watch it scale — Monitor your training and inference workloads across nodes in real-time. Zero code changes. Works with your existing training scripts. No Kubernetes expertise required. 7. "Know exactly where your compute is going" Track GPU spend per user, per team, across training and inference workloads. See who's using what, whether it aligns with business priorities, and where budget is burning on idle time. Priority-based scheduling means the most important jobs always run first. Managers get real-time visibility into usage and costs to make smarter infrastructure decisions. No more spreadsheets, no more guessing at the end of the month. Visual: Compute usage dashboard — team allocation pie chart, utilization over time graph, per-user GPU hours breakdown. 8. "Deploy anywhere" BYOC on any cloud provider — AWS, GCP, Azure — or on bare metal. Deployed in your VPC. Your data never leaves your infrastructure. For startups, go from cloud credits to a functional multi-node training setup with high bandwidth networking in under 20 minutes. For teams with existing reserved clusters, deploy on-prem or in your cloud. 9. Social Proof / Case Studies Testimonial 1 — Causal Labs: "Trainy allowed us to ramp up training from our local cluster to dozens of H100s in a hyperscaler in just 30 minutes using a simple 10-line config. By easily tapping into pools of on-demand compute, we could scale up and down according to our experiment workload — accelerating training without wasting budget on excess compute. It saved us weeks of time on GPU infrastructure." Result: 50% cost reduction vs AWS SageMaker. Testimonial 2: "ML training infra, delegated out. Existing frameworks take a lot of effort to get working and constantly debugging failures. Trainy takes care of that — reducing time spent on setup and reliability." Trust signals: YC-backed · customer logos (repeat/expand from hero) · 5M+ GPU hours managed. 10. FAQ Why Kubernetes? Kubernetes gives AI teams higher ROI on the same pool of compute. All top-tier research teams (OpenAI, Meta, etc.) have similar systems. With automated scheduling and cleanup, engineers never worry about GPU availability. Decision makers get visibility and control over cluster usage. How is Trainy different from Slurm? Trainy offers scheduling and resource sharing like Slurm, plus better workload isolation via containerization, integrated observability, and comprehensive health monitoring with automatic fault recovery. How does Pluto compare to W&B / Neptune? Pluto is built for responsiveness at scale — sub-second UI even with thousands of runs. Neptune-compatible API means you can migrate with one import change. Dual-logging lets you validate Pluto against your current tracker before cutting over. Open source, self-hostable. Is Pluto open source? Yes. Apache 2 licensed client, GPL server. Self-host with docker-compose in about a minute, or use managed hosting. Do I need to change my training code? No. Define workloads in YAML files, launch from CLI. Works with PyTorch, HuggingFace, JAX, Ray, and more. Zero code changes. 11. Final CTA Split block: Running GPU workloads? → Book a Demo Tracking experiments? → Start Free / Try Playground What changed from existing site Existing sectionWhat happened"Switch clouds anytime" (standalone)Folded into "Deploy anywhere" (section 8)"Scale beyond single machines" (standalone)Merged into training section (section 3)Framework compatibility (standalone)Mentioned in sections 3 and 6, not standalonePricing: On-Demand vs Reserved (section)Removed — no longer relevant, all reservedOn-Demand vs Reserved distinctionRemoved — all reserved nowFAQ: Data sources (Cloudflare R2)Cut — too in-the-weeds for landing page—Added: Inference section (4) — new—Added: Pluto / experiment tracking (5) — new—Added: FinOps per-user/team cost tracking (7) — expanded—Added: Social proof / testimonials (9) — new

HERO SECTION

GPU infra, solved.

Everything between buying GPUs and shipping models. Visual includes YAML config snippet flowing into training, inference, and experiment tracking cards.

PROBLEM STATEMENT

You bought GPUs. Now what?

Your team is spending weeks on scheduling, networking, and health checks instead of research. Or overpaying a managed platform to avoid it. Either way, your GPUs aren't working as hard as your team.

TRAINING

Scale training across hundreds of GPUs

Multi-node distributed training with RDMA-native networking. Priority-based scheduling, built-in health checks, automatic fault recovery. Works with PyTorch, HuggingFace, JAX, Ray, and more.

INFERENCE

Deploy and serve models

Inference scheduling on the same cluster, same YAML interface. Deploy serving endpoints with autoscaling, health checks, and reliability guarantees. One platform for training and inference.

EXPERIMENT TRACKING

Track every experiment without the lag

Pluto — experiment tracking built for responsiveness at scale. Neptune-compatible API, dual-logging support, MCP integration. Sub-second UI even with thousands of runs.

DEVELOPER EXPERIENCE

Launch your first job in 20 minutes

Write your config file, deploy with one command, watch it scale. Zero code changes, works with existing training scripts. No Kubernetes expertise required.

FINOPS

Know exactly where your compute is going

Track GPU spend per user, per team, across training and inference workloads. Real-time visibility into usage and costs. Priority-based scheduling ensures the most important jobs always run first.

DEPLOYMENT

Deploy anywhere

BYOC on any cloud provider — AWS, GCP, Azure — or on bare metal. Deployed in your VPC. Go from cloud credits to multi-node training setup in under 20 minutes.

SOCIAL PROOF

Trusted by top AI teams

Case studies from Causal Labs and others showing 50% cost reduction vs SageMaker. YC-backed, 5M+ GPU hours managed. Real testimonials from teams who scaled their infrastructure.

FAQ

Common questions answered

Why Kubernetes? How does it compare to Slurm? Is Pluto open source? Do I need to change my training code? Clear answers to help teams evaluate the platform.

FINAL CTA

Ready to scale your GPU workloads?

Split call-to-action: Running GPU workloads? Book a Demo. Tracking experiments? Try the Pluto Playground. Clear paths for both infrastructure and experiment tracking needs.
